newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Omni Industries aims to diversify for growth.
newsitem.headline: Omni Industries aims to diversify for growth.

text.p: Singapore electronics firm Omni Industries plans to sustain 15-20 percent growth over the next few years through diversification, company officials said on Tuesday.

Its business in computer and related peripherals and consumer electronics would be expanded to include design and manufacturing for telecommunications, automobiles, medical and instrumentation, they said.

"A major part of our projected 15-20 percent growth will come from diversification," group managing director Lee Kim Bock said at the company's initial public offering for listing on Singapore's second board, SESDAQ.
Omni offered 54 million shares at Singapore $0.45 each, with 40.5 million shares offered to the public and the balance of 13.5 million shares to be placed out privately.
The company says it expects to raise net proceeds of about $22.9 million to expand its factory capacity in China, develop markets in the United States and Europe and to diversify.
The group comprises 12 subsidiaries and one associate company engaged in plastic mould fabrication, contract manufacturing for circuit boards and distribution of electronic components.
Its strategy has been to provide a one-stop service to support manufacturers through the product development cycle.
"One-stop shortens the time to market and increases the customer's competitiveness. It is also cost efficient," Lee said.
Omni's sales have surged nearly tenfold from $15 million in 1991, when it was founded, to $140 million in 1995.
Performance has also turned around from a $4.0 million loss to a $6.0 million profit in 1995.
"The company's growth rate compares very favourably with the growth rate of recent IPO's listed," Richard Tan of placement agent OUB Bank told the news conference.
He said Omni's price earnings ratio of 13.6 times, at the low end of recently launched main board issues, was also "very competitive" with PE's of comparable companies.
The group's business was expected to expand this year helped by positive forecasts for the electronics industry, he said.
The Singapore government recently forecast output growth for the electronic sector would be between 10-15 percent this year compared with nine percent in 1996, Tan said.
